thread:
maria: Ok team — I want a single canonical traffic sim we can use for apples-to-apples kernel selection and batching heuristic tests. needs: deterministic QPS ramps, configurable microbursts, long-tail shaping, and KV cache warmup control.

alex: sounds good. do we force identical seq-lens and prompt mix across runs? otherwise apples-to-apples breaks.

maria: yes — canonical prompt corpus + fixed RNG seed. also canonicalize tokenization and pad rules.

jun: for KV cache behavior we should model sticky sessions + cold starts. propose a 3-phase run: cold-warm-hot. cold: no cache, warm: incremental KV fill, hot: steady-state hit-rate target.

sam: agree. also include occasional eviction storms to see how kernels react when KV misses spike. microburst pattern: 200ms spike to 5x QPS every 90s.

maria: sounds actionable. thinking config like: 
```json
{
  "seed": 42,
  "phases": [
    {"name":"cold","duration_s":60,"qps":10},
    {"name":"warm","duration_s":180,"qps_ramp":{"start":10,"end":50}},
    {"name":"hot","duration_s":600,"qps":50,"burst_pattern":"sawtooth"}
  ],
  "microburst":{"interval_s":90,"multiplier":5,"duration_ms":200},
  "kv_profile":{"initial_hit":0.0,"target_hit":0.85,"eviction_event_s":300} 
}
```

alex: nice. add an option to pin kernel and batch-policy per run so we can automate pairwise comparisons: kernel=A+batch=b vs kernel=B+batch=c. outputs should include p50/p95/p99 and token-per-second.

jun: for long-tail shaping we should skew the latency target distribution by sampling request interarrival from a heavy-tailed dist (pareto alpha=1.8) while keeping mean qps fixed. that produces realistic tail without changing avg throughput.

sam: also capture per-request KV-hit metadata so we can slice latency by hit/miss. small snippet from last profiling run: 
```
[profile] kernel=fast-attn v1 | batch=32 | p50=23ms p95=94ms p99=310ms | kv_hit_rate=0.78
[profile] kernel=alt-opt v2  | batch=16 | p50=26ms p95=110ms p99=420ms | kv_hit_rate=0.80
```

maria: those logs make the case — kernel choice interacts w/ batch size and kv hit ratio. plan: bake this sim into the replay harness so we can replay real traces under identical generator settings.

alex: question: how do we make the generator deterministic across OSes? RNG seed alone won't cover scheduling jitter. need to run inside a single-threaded harness for timing control or use virtual clock.

jun: agree. use virtual clock + event queue in the harness. time.sleep in harness => nondet. virtual clock ensures identical interarrival.

sam: for CI runs, limit duration to shorter canonical scenario (cold->warm->short-hot) and export artifact bucket with raw traces, per-request metadata, and aggregate CSVs. include a small reproducible script that pins kernels and runs n=3 repeats.

maria: OK I'll draft the README and config schema today. action items:
- maria: write canonical prompt corpus + tokenization rules
- alex: add kernel/batch pinning to replay harness CLI
- jun: implement virtual-clock driver and KV-profile phase support
- sam: add microburst/eviction scenarios + CI job

infra-bot: CI run queued: traffic-sim/canonical-proto (id: run-2026-53). will post artifacts when done. :gear:
